# E0510: property that performs `io`

A property runs on generated cases and gives the same verdict on every run, so it can't read or write the world. Remove the `print`.

- Rule: [`tests.property-io`](../../reference/19-tools.md#tests.property-io)
- Reported at: the first call that performs `io`.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `types` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0510:1
/// prop: |a: i64, b: i64| { print("{a} {b}"); add(a, b) == add(b, a) }
fn add(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { a +% b }
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
/// prop: |a: i64, b: i64| add(a, b) == add(b, a)
fn add(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { a +% b }
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0510_property_that_performs_io.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0510_property_that_performs_io.lt):

```text
── PROPERTY THAT PERFORMS `io` ── E0510_property_that_performs_io.lt:1:30  [E0510]

This performs `io`, which a property can't:

  1 │ /// prop: |a: i64, b: i64| { print("{a} {b}"); add(a, b) == add(b, a) }
    │                              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

A property runs on generated cases and gives the same verdict on every run, so
it can't read or write the world. Remove the `print`.

To fix it, remove the `print`:

  1 │ /// prop: |a: i64, b: i64| { print("{a} {b}"); add(a, b) == add(b, a) }
    │                              ------------------
```
